title: Tuning Reverse Proxy Buffers to Prevent 502s
prompt: Your Nginx 1.24 reverse proxy fronts an OAuth2/OIDC SSO gateway and a GraphQL API at 6,000 RPS. After a product release added 45 fine-grained RBAC claims to the session JWT cookie, 6.5% of requests fail with `502 Bad Gateway`. Nginx error logs show `upstream sent too big header while reading response header from upstream` and `400 Request Header Or Cookie Too Large`. Each Nginx node has 16 GB RAM and handles up to 10,000 concurrent connections. Fix both the immediate 502 outage and the underlying token bloat without risking Nginx OOM.

spark.summary: Oversized OAuth2 JWTs and cookies (> 8 KB) overflow Nginx's default 4K/8K `proxy_buffer_size`, triggering `502 Bad Gateway` for 6.5% of SSO and GraphQL requests.
spark.keyTakeaway: When traffic spikes expose hidden coupling, align `proxy_buffer_size` / `proxy_buffers` to 16 KB–32 KB for immediate relief, then eliminate cookie/JWT bloat using opaque Redis-backed reference tokens (< 128 bytes).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Three common misconfigurations leave `502`s unfixed: **Increasing `client_max_body_size`**: Only governs request *body* size, never HTTP headers.
